design.description: Owner-synced design: three layers, enforcement levels, rejected options, open questions

env.toolchain: Python 3.12+, uv; jsonschema for specpack validation

plan.approach: Schema first (additive 0.3 with format enum), then the slice resolver (pure machine behavior), then pinning and rebase, then handout verification for links and artifacts, then coverage reporting, then docs. The spec rides on 0.2 so the loop can run it before 0.3 exists.

decisions.because: The links say what a task answers, the slice says what those things say, the context block says what world state it was planned against; one mechanism cannot carry all three without either embedding or losing pinning.
decisions.decision: Handoff is three layers: TRACE links (declarative), slice expansion (resolution at handout), context block (pinning).

decisions.because: Embedding duplicates reality and drifts silently; pinning everything generates rebase noise that trains workers to ignore rebase.
decisions.decision: Reference, never embed; pin only touch; read, wiki, and digestless links stay advisory.

decisions.because: Owner direction: context may point at Confluence, blogs, and other URLs, and may carry plain text; pack git history already records authorship.
decisions.decision: notes are plain strings (provenance via git blame) and links accept external URLs or repo-relative paths with optional sha256 and retrieved_at.

decisions.because: Notes must not become an embedded shadow spec; that is the waterfall trap the harness refuses.
decisions.decision: Promote-to-node rule: when a note becomes load-bearing it is promoted to a decision, constraint, or clarification, and the note shrinks to a pointer.

decisions.because: Hard checks would block legitimate doc-only tasks and freeze work on open questions that bounded slices can route around.
decisions.decision: Context completeness, note length, env absence, and open questions are coverage-tier reports, not violations.

decisions.because: The worker session is the fence; acceptance-time pinning would wall every pack against normal code motion.
decisions.decision: Pin at loom next: digests are written at first handout and verified against the current bytes at every handout; drift since the last pin refuses the handout.

decisions.because: Re-hashing bytes is mechanical, but a drift is a signal the plan no longer matches the code. The agent proposes the fix; the human accepts it. This is the harness trust rule applied to rebase. The claim is a shape check like A7: git and review carry the truth.
decisions.decision: An agent may re-pin only with owner approval at the drift: the agent shows the drift (paths, pinned vs current) and the remedies (re-pin and continue, or replan); the owner approves; loom rebase --approved-by human:<owner> records the approval claim. Git history is the provenance record.

designs.detail: One schema file: format becomes enum [specpack/0.2, specpack/0.3]; task gains optional context (touch with path/sha256/why, read with path/why, wiki cids, links with url/why/sha256/retrieved_at, notes strings, commands with cmd/expect_exit); verify gains optional steps (run/expect_exit/expect_contains); pack gains optional env (build/test/lint/toolchain). Paths in touch and read are relative to the git root containing the pack; links may be URLs or repo-relative paths.
designs.title: Schema 0.3 delta

designs.detail: slice_for stops flattening: in-slice nodes render as full objects; designs expand one hop through addresses to their FRs with a via marker; every accepted decision enters the slice; prerequisite tasks contribute detail, produces, and evidence; the handout carries a plan prelude (approach, stack, env when present).
designs.title: Slice resolver

designs.detail: At handout: touch entries without sha256 get pinned (first handout); entries with sha256 are verified against the file bytes; any mismatch returns status needs_rebase with a drift list and the task is not handed out. loom rebase <dir> --task re-pins current digests; git history of the pack is the provenance record (no clock fields).
designs.title: Pin and rebase flow

designs.detail: links carrying sha256 and artifacts carrying sha256 are verified at handout; a mismatch refuses the handout with the offending entries named. Advisory links (no digest) pass through unchecked.
designs.title: Handout digest verification

designs.detail: alignment coverage gains a context section: tasks missing detail, tasks missing touch, notes longer than a threshold, env absence, open questions while tasks are ready. Printed by loom check; never a violation.
designs.title: Coverage reporter extension

clarifications.question: Pin moment: at loom next (re-pin each handout, refuse drift since the last pin) or at plan acceptance (stricter, explicit rebase wall)?
clarifications.answer: Pin at loom next (option A). The work session is the fence; the human accepted D-6 on 2026-10-08.

clarifications.question: Who may re-pin drifted digests: any agent (with git as the provenance record) or a human only?
clarifications.answer: Any agent may re-pin, but only after owner approval at the drift: agent shows guidance, owner approves, rebase records --approved-by human:<owner> (option A with an approval gate, accepted 2026-10-08).

constraints.text: Additive only: no 0.2 field changes shape, no field moves, no new required fields.
No new runtime dependencies and no imports between loom_kit and okf_kit in either direction.
A1 to A7 semantics unchanged; all new reporting is coverage-tier (reported, never blocking).
Determinism preserved: sorted lists, canonical digests, no clocks outside evidence rows.

out_of_scope: loom L2 (automated wiki retrieval from context.wiki)
mirroring auth-gated URLs into artifacts automatically
UI or HTML renders of the context block

scenarios.then: zero validation errors; the 0.3 fixture with a full context block also validates
scenarios.when: it is validated against the updated single schema

requirements.text: The schema MUST accept specpack/0.3 as an additive extension of 0.2: an optional per-task context block (touch, read, wiki, links, notes, commands), optional verify steps, and a pack-level env block. Every 0.2 pack MUST remain valid.

scenarios.given: a task that implements a design which addresses a requirement
scenarios.then: the slice carries the requirement text with a via marker naming the design, and accepted decisions are present
scenarios.when: loom next hands the task out

requirements.text: The frozen context at handout MUST carry full node bodies: requirement text behind implemented designs (with a via marker), prerequisite detail, produced files, and evidence, plus every accepted decision and the plan prelude.

scenarios.given: a todo task with pinned touch digests
scenarios.then: next returns status needs_rebase naming the drift and the task stays todo
scenarios.when: a touch file changes and loom next runs

requirements.text: loom next MUST pin touch digests at handout and MUST refuse a drifted task with status needs_rebase instead of handing it out; loom rebase MUST re-pin.
The machine MUST verify sha256 digests on links and artifacts at handout when present; a mismatch MUST refuse the handout.
loom next MUST render verify steps and the env block in the handout; the record-time A6 rule (every command exit 0) MUST NOT change.
loom check MUST report context completeness, long notes, env absence, and open questions as coverage-tier output, never as violations; A1 to A7 semantics MUST NOT change.
The schema primer and the wiki loom page MUST describe 0.3, and the repo MUST end okf-fresh with no stale anchors.

stories.so: I can act on a spec I did not write, without its authors present
stories.want: a self-contained handout with spec, design, rationale, code anchors, and exact checks

spec.why: A pack built by one team must be executable by a fresh session. The 0.2 handout flattens nodes to one-liners, never reaches decisions, and pins nothing about the code it targets.

tasks.detail: Extend specpack.schema.json additively per DES-1: format enum [specpack/0.2, specpack/0.3]; $defs for contextEntry-ish shapes (touch {path, sha256, why}, read {path, why}, links {url, why, sha256, retrieved_at}, notes strings, commands {cmd, expect_exit}); task.context; verify.steps {run, expect_exit, expect_contains}; root env {build, test, lint, toolchain} all optional strings. Loader already accepts any specpack/* format tag; validate() uses the one vendored schema so no loader change is needed beyond tests. New tests: a 0.3 fixture with a full context block validates; the 0.2 example pack still validates with zero errors.
